chunks: My father narrated to us, may God have mercy upon him, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may God be pleased with him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, who said: I heard Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) say:
Whoever of my friends visits me, recognizing my rightfulness, I will intercede for him on the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Ar-Rida with recognition of his rightfulness?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam Ar-Rida (a.s.) links the efficacy of Ziyarah (visitation) directly to 'Ma'rifah' (gnostic recognition) of his divine station, a key concept in Shia theology. This establishes that physical presence is secondary to spiritual awareness, ensuring that the intercession (Shafa'ah) granted is not merely ritualistic but rooted in true theological understanding. The narration underscores the Imam's role as an intercessor whose authority is recognized by his 'Awliya' (friends/saints).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 66-16 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God have mercy upon him - and Muhammad ibn Al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Waleed - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Talib, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bezanti, “I heard Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) say, ‘
I will intercede on behalf of all of my friends who visit me recognizing my rightfulness on the Resurrection Day.”
